text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Parliament will vote today on the 6,433 billion Lebanese pounds ($4 billion) state budget for 1997.
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir said parliamentary debate showed that there is no planning and no accounting in the pubic administration.
-Saudi Arabian Airlines resumed flights to Beirut on Saturday after a halt of nearly 15 years.
-The Bank of Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves rose $104.62 million in the second half of January to $6,140.55 million, according to the central bank's bi-monthly balance sheet.
-Israeli shelling on suspected pro-Iranian Hizbollah positions in south Lebanon.
-Schoolteachers union demands government pay overdue salary increases.
-Former Hizbollah chief Toufayli said Prime Minister Hariri is an American representative in Lebanon.
-February shopping festival brings out crowds in Beirut.
